name: Ante Pavelić
role: Founder of the Ustaše (1929) and Poglavnik of the Independent State of Croatia (1941–1945)
summary: Croatian nationalist lawyer who founded the Ustaše to win a Croatian state by any means, including terror, and then ruled the Axis-sponsored Independent State of Croatia as a one-man dictator by decree. His regime enacted racial laws against Jews and Roma, banned Cyrillic and carried out mass killing of Serbs, Jews and Roma. He ideologically stressed Croatian blood, the peasantry and a religious family life.

class-collaboration.rationale: The principles say all classes of the Croatian people form one unified whole defined by blood, which puts national unity above class division.

conscription.rationale: Britannica reports the Ustaša state conscripted an army to join the Axis powers and fight the resistance.

death-penalty.rationale: He decreed the death penalty for high treason and mandatory death by firing squad for a list of offences under the courts-martial decree.

defeat-communism.rationale: The Ustaša state conscripted an army to fight the resistance movements and at the end hoped for Western backing in the fight against communism.

democracy-best.rationale: He governed as a dictator, issuing law by decree and ruling through courts-martial rather than by electoral consent, as reported by Britannica.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The Aryan-blood decree prohibited marriage between Aryans and Jews or other non-Aryans, and criminalised extramarital sexual relations across the line, with prison and in grave cases death.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The principles say the material wealth of the Croatian state belongs to the people, who alone may possess and use it, and that only those of Croatian origin decide state affairs.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The courts-martial decree replaced ordinary courts for listed offences with death by firing squad within three hours of verdict and no appeal; a decree of 17 April 1941 created special three-member people's courts with expedited procedure.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Britannica reports his state's army was raised to join the Axis powers, i.e. he joined a permanent military bloc.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The decrees of 30 April 1941 stripped Jews and Roma of citizenship and imposed legal disabilities by racial descent, the opposite of equal rights before the law.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Citizenship and political rights were limited to nationals of Aryan descent, and the racial decrees defined Jews and Roma out of the community (citizenship provision, racial affiliation decree).

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The Aryan-blood decree legally forbade Jews and non-Aryans to employ certain women, and forbade marriages and relations, so private choices of whom to deal with were restricted by law, not left unrestricted.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The principles hold that the Croats conquered and permanently made the land theirs, that nobody may claim any of its provinces, and that only those of Croatian blood decide in the Croatian state.

minority-language-support.rationale: He banned Cyrillic script throughout the state in public and private life, and the language decree forbade non-Croatian names for shops and companies.

mutual-intelligibility-defines-language.rationale: The language decree declares Croatian not identical with, not a dialect of and not related to any other nation's language, which rejects treating mutually understandable varieties as one language.

night-watchman-state.rationale: His state legislated on language, naming of shops, citizenship by race, marriage and employment, far beyond protection from physical violence.

one-party-rule.rationale: The reference entry reports the Ustaša regime imposed a one-party system and outlawed all other parties, including the Croatian Peasant Party.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The key laws of 1941 were issued by decree of the Poglavnik, with a legislative commission attached to him, and no parliament made them.

political-violence-legitimate.rationale: Britannica reports the Ustaše under Pavelić ran terrorist training camps, attempted a rebellion in 1932 and took part in the 1934 assassination of King Alexander.

population-transfer.rationale: The regime pursued expulsion of Serbs, per the reference entry, and the USHMM records deportation of Serbs, Roma and Jews.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The language decree treats the Croatian language as the public welfare of the Croatian people and protects its 'purity' by law.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The defence provision punished acts that 'violated' Croatian honour even in the past and was applied by courts appointed by the minister, and the courts-martial decree allowed no remedy against verdicts; this is rule by retroactive decree, not standing public law.

purge-loanwords.rationale: The language decree forbade foreign words that do not fit the spirit of Croatian and ordered the language 'cleansed'.

racial-franchise.rationale: Political rights belonged only to 'citizens', defined as nationals of Aryan descent who had shown loyalty to the Croatian people's liberation aims; this reserves the vote-bearing status by race, though to a wider group than one ethnic group.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The decree barred non-Aryans from employing Aryan women under 45 and from displaying Croatian flags and colours, and barred intermarriage; this is statutory racial separation in everyday life, though not a full segregation code.

remove-other-ethnic-groups-from-country.rationale: The reference entry reports a policy of expulsion, extermination and conversion of Serbs, Britannica says the aim was a more purely Croatian state, and the USHMM records deportations to camps.

revolution-legitimate.rationale: Britannica reports that the Ustaše tried to incite a peasant rebellion in northern Dalmatia in 1932 to bring down Yugoslav rule.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The principles make the peasantry the foundation and sole constituent of the Croatian nation and place its moral strength in village family life.

separated-powers.rationale: He combined head of state, prime minister and foreign minister in his own hands, appointed the justice minister who appointed the special courts, and ruled by decree.

single-official-language.rationale: The language decree declared Croatian the language of public life, banned foreign names for businesses, and Cyrillic was banned; other languages were not abolished everywhere.

state-harmful.rationale: He founded the Ustaše to establish a Croatian state, and then headed that state as Poglavnik.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Britannica reports that his state conscripted an army to join the Axis powers, one of the rival blocs.

strong-leader.rationale: He took the post of Poglavnik, personally held the head of state and foreign affairs, appointed all ministers himself and issued laws by decree.

suppress-opposition.rationale: His decrees made any act harming Croatian honour or endangering the state high treason punishable by death, and created courts-martial; the 26 June 1941 command threatened court-martial for rumours and camps for Jews.

traditional-family.rationale: The principles state that the essence of the Croatian people's moral strength is an orderly and religious family life.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The principles state the Croatian name has been unchanged for 1,300 years and that the Croatian state was preserved through the centuries and never abandoned.
